model_annotation: This bar chart compares the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms generated by a base model, Mistralv0.2-Base, and its fine-tuned variants across six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents the negative log probability, scaled from -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher probability (better performance). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, each corresponding to a group of bars. Within each group, the first bar (light blue) represents the base model’s performance, while the subsequent bars (in shades of orange to dark brown) represent the performance of models fine-tuned on each of the six specialties, as indicated by the legend. For each specialty, the fine-tuned model on that specialty typically achieves the lowest negative log probability (highest probability), suggesting improved performance on its own domain. For example, in the "Cardio" group, the base model has a negative log probability of approximately -22.2, while the Cardio-fine-tuned model reaches about -26.8. Similarly, in "Pediatrics," the base model scores around -22.5, while the Pediatrics-fine-tuned model reaches approximately -26.5. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning improves performance within the target specialty, with the base model consistently performing worse across all specialties. The bars are arranged in groups by specialty, and the fine-tuned models are ordered according to the legend, with colors ranging from light orange (Cardio) to dark brown (Pediatrics). The chart does not include error bars or statistical significance markers, and all bars are of uniform width and aligned at the baseline.
